Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). We work modulo \(p\).

For \(m<k\le p-1\), we have \(p\le 2k<2p\), so \(p\mid (2k)!\) but \(p\nmid (k!)^2\). Hence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p
\]

for \(m<k\le 2026\). Therefore the sum only involves \(0\le k\le m\).

We use the congruence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv (-4)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p
\]

for \(0\le k\le m\). It is easy to prove by induction:

\[
\binom{2k+2}{k+1}
=
\binom{2k}{k}\frac{2(2k+1)}{k+1},
\]

and

\[
(-4)^{k+1}\binom{m}{k+1}
=
(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}\frac{-4(m-k)}{k+1}.
\]

The factors match because

\[
2(2k+1)+4(m-k)=4m+2=2(2m+1)\equiv 0\pmod p.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{m}\binom{2k}{k}x^k
\equiv
\sum_{k=0}^{m}\binom{m}{k}(-4)^kx^k
=
(1-4x)^m
\pmod p.
\]

Let

\[
P(x)=(1-4x)^m.
\]

The desired sum is

\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{2026} k\binom{2k}{k}2^k
=
2P'(2).
\]

Since

\[
P'(x)=-4m(1-4x)^{m-1},
\]

we get

\[
2P'(2)=-8m(-7)^{m-1}.
\]

Also \(P(2)=(-7)^m\). Since \(2m+1\equiv 0\pmod p\), we have \(m\equiv -\frac12\pmod p\), so

\[
2P'(2)\equiv -4P(2)/7\pmod p.
\]

Now

\[
P(2)=(-7)^m=\left(\frac{-7}{p}\right)
\]

by Euler’s criterion. Compute the Legendre symbol:

\[
\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)=-1
\]

because \(p\equiv 3\pmod 4\). Also, since \(p\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and \(7\equiv 3\pmod 4\),

\[
\left(\frac{7}{p}\right)=-\left(\frac{p}{7}\right).
\]

Now \(p=2027\equiv 4\pmod 7\), so \(\left(\frac{p}{7}\right)=\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)=1\). Hence

\[
\left(\frac{7}{p}\right)=-1,
\]

and therefore

\[
\left(\frac{-7}{p}\right)=(-1)(-1)=1.
\]

Thus \(P(2)\equiv 1\pmod{2027}\), and

\[
S\equiv -\frac{4}{7}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Finally,

\[
7\cdot 289=2023\equiv -4\pmod{2027},
\]

so

\[
-\frac{4}{7}\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
